newsitem.title: FRANCE: French judge sends BA Algeria protest to new court.
newsitem.headline: French judge sends BA Algeria protest to new court.

text.p: A French judge sent British Airways to a different court on Tuesday to pursue its bid to win tighter security at Paris's biggest airport after the state airline of violence-torn Algeria resumed flights.

A British Airways spokeswoman said the court at Versailles, west of Paris, had declared itself "geographically incompetent" to judge the suit brought by the airline on Monday seeking more security at Roissy-Charles de Gaulle airport north of the capital.
"The dossier has been transmitted to the administrative court in Melun," she said. Melun is south-east of Paris.

British Airways has been closing its counters at Charles de Gaulle airport for several hours a day since the weekend after Air Algerie resumed flights to and from Paris after a two-year break, opening check-in desks alongside those of British Airways.

The British airline said later in a statement that it regretted the judge's decision and intended to pursue its drive "to ensure the same security measures are instituted (at Roissy) as already exist for Air Algerie at other French airports".
British Airways is carrying out check-in operations on the terminal roof and in a nearby hotel. Passengers have to carry luggage aboard or have it sent directly to their destination.
About 60,000 people have died in Algeria in violence sparked by the cancellation of January 1992 elections which Moslem fundamentalists were set to win.

Airport authorities say security is already extra-tight and say that no other airlines have protested. British Airways says Air Algerie has separate baggage check-ins at other French airports -- Marseille, Lyon, Nice and Toulouse.
Troops already patrol the airport after a wave of bombings in France by Algerian Moslem extremists in 1995.
Air Algerie suspended flights to Paris two years ago in protest at being forced to use a remote terminal after Moslem radicals hijacked an Air France plane in Algiers at Christmas 1995.
The four hijackers killed three passengers and were themselves killed by French commandos who stormed the plane in Marseille.
